changes: No changes to persons, relations, date or place. Notes expanded: 'dayakā' may give the year the play was composed or staged, not the year it was copied.

notes: The catalogue lists King Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur, but he is not named in the quoted colophon. The catalogue probably names him as the play's author or patron. The only date is 'saṃvat 807 madārasāharana dayakā' ('Madālasāharaṇa made, saṃvat 807'). The era is not stated. NS fits because the script is Newari and the year falls in Jitāmitra Malla's reign (c. NS 793–816). 'dayakā' (Newari, 'made') could mark when the play was composed or staged rather than when this copy was made, so treating 807 as the copying date is uncertain. The rest of the quoted text is song and stage material (rāgas, entries of Kambala, Aśvatara and others; Gālava, Viṣṇu and Mahādeva) and drum syllables. None of these are persons connected with the copy.
